turn.context: Playbook §7: the low-commitment trial first. Scoped day by day.

text: Here is the trial, day by day. Nothing changes for the first three days, so we get the ward’s own starting times.
Then the changes come in two steps. On days 12 to 14 we read the numbers together.
chat.pointer: Pick a day, or play the two weeks. The board shows who acts and what is recorded.
chat.invite: Next, we can see who has to agree before day 1.
chat.note: Three quiet days first. Then we know what changed.
prompts: Who has to agree to this?
What changes on the ward, step by step?
Which ward should we start on?

blocks.title: Fourteen days on one ward
blocks.deck: No new staff and no new system. The ward phone and a one-tap form are enough.

ward.label: The ward whose consultants decide latest
ward.note: They gain the most, so the change shows fastest. You pick the ward.

needs: The one-tap form on a ward phone
One person to record the times

phases.title: Record today’s times
phases.what: Nothing changes yet. The ward records when each patient is ready to go and when they leave.

phases.title: The evening round starts it
phases.what: Doctors mark likely discharges on the evening round. The night nurse starts the papers and the bill.
records: Papers ready by the morning round

phases.title: Insurance and family the night before
phases.what: The insurance desk sends its request the evening before. The family hears the leaving time that night.

phases.title: Read the numbers
phases.what: Compare the trial days with days 1 to 3. Then choose: adjust and try again, or spread to more wards.

blocks.condition: Goals for each measure are set on day 3, from the ward’s own times. None are guessed now.
